title: General Information
intro: A little journey through the world of chess.
origin.title: First steps in India
origin.body: Chaturanga, an ancestor of chess, was played in India around the 6th century. It began a long journey towards the game we know today.
journey.title: A game travels the world
journey.body: The game reached Persia, then spread through the Islamic world to Europe. Many communities helped chess develop.
rules.title: Towards modern chess
rules.body: In late 15th-century Europe, queens and bishops gained stronger moves. The game grew closer to modern chess.
championship.title: The age of championships
championship.body: Steinitz won the first official world championship match in 1886. The international chess federation, FIDE, was founded in 1924.
steinitz.body: He became the first official world chess champion in 1886. He valued coordinated pieces and strong positions.
lasker.body: He was world champion from 1894 to 1921. His 27 years as champion gave him a special place in chess history.
capablanca.body: The Cuban master was world champion from 1921 to 1927. He was known for clear play and great skill in endgames.
menchik.body: She won the first Women’s World Championship in 1927. She remained champion until 1944 and inspired later players.
kasparov.body: He defeated Karpov to become world champion in 1985. He held the classical title until 2000 and was known for attacking play and deep preparation.
karpov.body: He was world champion from 1975 to 1985 and FIDE world champion from 1993 to 1999. He was known for patient play and making the most of small advantages.
fischer.body: The American master defeated Boris Spassky to become world champion in 1972. He held the title until 1975.
anand.body: The Indian master became FIDE world champion in 2000. He held the unified world title from 2007 to 2013.
carlsen.body: The Norwegian master was classical world champion from 2013 to 2023. He is known for making the most of small chances, especially in endgames.
polgar.body: The Hungarian master became the first woman to reach the world’s overall top ten. Her success inspired girls to aim for the highest levels of chess.
